You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: What image-grounded evidence, if any, establishes progress on relocating the requested mug to the headphones' right?
node.criteria: pass: Visible evidence establishes some requested relocation progress; describe the concrete change and whether it establishes an incomplete or completed result. fail: The images establish no requested relocation progress, such as the identifiable target remaining unchanged while only unrelated objects or scene details change. unknown: The evidence cannot distinguish requested progress from unrelated changes or ambiguous object correspondence. Neither a change of any kind nor a right-side unidentified mug alone establishes progress. Do not require a reconstructed editing operation or a particular trajectory.
node.binding: Compare source and edited images directly, tracking the requested source mug using multiple visible features and scene correspondence. Assess progress toward the requested relative placement rather than arbitrary displacement. Distinguish evidence of relocation from uncertain disappearance, added objects, and appearance changes; these possibilities are hypotheses, not predetermined findings. Inspect independently even if endpoint correspondence is unresolved, and report any independently grounded progress evidence without inventing continuity.

node_traces.evidence: The source has one distinctive light-blue mug left of the headphones. In the edited image, that mug is not clearly identifiable: there is a blue blurred shape at the left and two small white mugs, with no reliable visual correspondence establishing that the source mug was relocated to the headphones’ right. The apparent changes therefore do not establish requested relocation progress.

fulfillment: The binding is too generic to preserve target identity: the source mug is the distinctive light-blue mug with a curved handle, initially left of the headphones. Make the node explicitly compare that source object across the before/after images, rather than treating any mug-like object on the right as the target. But do not let identity ambiguity erase independently visible progress: the edited image shows a mug-like object left of the headphones and another to their right, while the original blue mug appears blurred at far left. The current traces do not establish which edited object is the original, so uncertainty is warranted; the reference label “partial” is an aggregate constraint, not proof that either mug is the target. Improve the node’s criterion to distinguish grounded evidence of partial movement from mere additions or ambiguous correspondence, and preserve unknown when neither is established. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; the issue is visual identity/evidence ambiguity, not a reason to force a label or lower confidence.
